title: Metrics Pipeline
summary: Multi-tenant time-series ingest with per-series logical clocks, retained raw samples, and 60/3600-unit rollups.
source: HLD Handbook Metrics Pipeline case study, adapted by this repository's bounded challenge contract.
requirements: Address each series by tenant, metric, and structural labels.
Ingest samples using the series clock to reject future, expired, or previously accepted timestamps.
Retain accepted raw samples for 300 clock units and aggregate them into 60- and 3600-wide buckets.
nonfunctional: Reads and ingest for one series must not examine other series.
Ingest is bounded per sample; series-info reads are bounded; clock advancement may process expirations on that series.
constraints: Clock starts at 0 and only increases; timestamps and values are signed 64-bit integers.
Raw retained iff timestamp + 300 > clock; rollups retained iff bucket-start + width + 7200 > clock.
Rollups complete at bucket-start + width <= clock; complete buckets can still receive admissible late samples.
invariants: First accepted sample per series/timestamp wins; rejection does not reserve a timestamp.
Raw expiry never subtracts from rollups or cumulative admission counters.
Each aggregate records count, sum, min, max of all accepted samples in that bucket.
acceptance: Queries return ascending results in requested half-open ranges.
Rollup query returns only complete, retained, nonempty buckets.
Stale/equal clock advances do nothing; an unseen series reports zero clock and counters.
environment: Durable PState; synchronize asynchronous writes before reads
interfaces: MetricsPipeline: advance-clock!, ingest-sample!, get-series-info, query-raw, query-rollup
create-module returns module and wrap-client; client implements Synchronizable
decisions: Canonical structural SeriesKey [tenant metric labels] is the partition key.
Microbatch topology owns durable series state; separate query topologies serve raw and rollup ranges.
60-wide buckets use subindexed sorted maps; small 3600-wide maps remain plain maps.
tradeoffs: Per-series colocation enables atomic local ingest and bounded single-series reads.
Clock advancement performs explicit expiry work; wider aggregates preserve expired raw contributions.
seam: The contract defines deterministic metrics storage, not scraping, PromQL, alerting, compression, HA deduplication, or capacity.
pstates: $$series keyed by SeriesKey; clock, counters, raw, buckets-60, buckets-3600

write: Client canonicalizes labels into SeriesKey and appends AdvanceClock or IngestSample.
*series-events routes by hash of :series to the owning task; metrics microbatch updates $$series locally.
Accepted ingest stores raw value, folds both rollups, and increments accepted; rejection increments its matching counter.
Clock advance prunes expired raw and rollup keys for that series.
read: Client invokes query-raw or query-rollup; each query topology hashes SeriesKey to its owning task before local range select.
query-raw range-selects retained timestamp entries; query-rollup computes eligible bucket-start range and selects the matching width's state.
get-series-info is a direct PState select, not a query topology.
flow.partition: SeriesKey = [tenant metric canonical labels]; depot hash-by :series and query |hash route the key to the $$series partition.

caveat: Logical time and integer values only. Production scraping, compression, alerting, high availability and retention infrastructure are excluded.

title: Ad-Click Aggregation
summary: Campaign-scoped exactly-once click audit and 60-unit window aggregation with late-event, fraud, validity, and billing dispositions.
source: HLD Handbook Ad-Click Aggregation case study, adapted by this repository's bounded challenge contract.
requirements: Record each campaign/request ID once with an immutable audit record and disposition.
Aggregate counted clicks by tumbling window and joint geo/device breakdown.
Advance a campaign watermark monotonically; only billed clicks contribute spend.
nonfunctional: Per-click processing is bounded independent of click, window, and campaign counts.
Campaign reads are isolated from other campaigns; range reads scale with windows and breakdowns returned.
constraints: Windows are 60 units; a window ending at E closes at watermark >= E + 120.
Disposition precedence: closed window late, then fraud, then invalid, otherwise billed.
Request IDs are campaign-scoped; replay has no effect, including after closure.
invariants: First audit record and observed watermark are permanent.
Fraud and invalid are counted but not billed; late is audited but not counted.
Clicks = billed-clicks + invalid-clicks + fraud-clicks; billed-spend sums billed spend only.
acceptance: get-window is nil absent counted clicks; get-windows returns populated windows in ascending order over [start,end).
Stale watermark updates do nothing; future timestamps are admitted normally.
Totals and [geo device] breakdown counters remain consistent.
environment: Durable campaign PState; async writes synchronized before reads
interfaces: AdClickAggregation: advance-watermark!, record-click!, get-watermark, get-request, get-window, get-windows
create-module returns module and wrap-client; client implements Synchronizable
decisions: Partition complete event stream and campaign state by campaign-id.
Microbatch click-accounting owns campaign watermark, request audit, and window aggregates.
Use one query topology windows-in-range for window and range reads.
tradeoffs: Campaign colocation allows replay check, disposition, audit, and aggregate update together.
The shared range query pages sorted window entries to bound reads; each returned window requires its breakdown read.
seam: Fraud detection is caller-supplied; Kafka/Flink, impressions/CTR, pacing, OLAP, reconciliation, privacy policy, and capacity are excluded.
pstates: $$campaigns keyed by campaign-id; watermark, requests, windows and geo/device breakdown
queries: windows-in-range (query topology; serves get-window and get-windows via foreign-invoke-query)
get-watermark and get-request are direct foreign-select-one reads on $$campaigns

write: Client appends AdvanceWatermark or RecordClick to *campaign-events.
hash-by :campaign-id routes events to campaign owner; click-accounting microbatch enforces replay check and disposition.
First arrival writes audit; only billed/invalid/fraud updates window totals and [geo device] counters.
read: get-window/get-windows invoke windows-in-range query topology; it routes by |hash campaign-id, range-selects windows, and locally selects each breakdown.
get-request and get-watermark directly select one key/field from $$campaigns; no query topology.
flow.partition: campaign-id is both depot hash key and query |hash key; all request and window state for a campaign is colocated in $$campaigns.

caveat: Accounting and audit state only. Ingestion infrastructure, fraud classification, OLAP and billing delivery are excluded.

title: Distributed Job Scheduler
summary: Bounded immutable DAG execution with idempotent claim decisions, expiring worker leases, increasing fencing tokens, and one immutable completion result.
source: HLD Handbook Distributed Job Scheduler case study, adapted by this repository's bounded challenge contract.
requirements: Accept only nonempty acyclic DAGs of at most 32 nodes with all dependency references resolved.
Make nodes claimable only after dependencies succeed; grant 10-unit leases with monotonically increasing per-node tokens.
Record every new claim decision and accept completion only from the current unexpired lease holder.
nonfunctional: Operations may scale with the single DAG of at most 32 nodes, not other executions, claims, or workers.
Reads for one execution must not inspect another execution's state.
constraints: Execution clock starts at 0 and is monotonic; lease valid iff clock < expiry.
Claim IDs are execution-scoped idempotency keys, including denials made for unknown executions.
Completion is immutable and an expired worker cannot complete even before another claim.
invariants: DAG is immutable after accepted submission; rejected DAG leaves no execution.
Token increases on each grant; stable effect-id is [execution-id node-id].
At most one result is recorded per logical node effect; external effect execution is not guaranteed exactly once.
acceptance: Claim denial order is unknown execution, unknown node, success, dependencies, active lease, then grant.
At expiry equality a lease is invalid and node is ready unless succeeded or dependencies remain incomplete.
Execution is success iff all nodes succeeded; claimable-node list is ascending.
environment: Durable execution state; writes to same execution applied in invocation order
interfaces: JobScheduler: submit-execution!, advance-clock!, claim!, complete!, get-execution, get-node, get-claim, get-claimable-nodes
create-module returns module and wrap-client; client implements Synchronizable
decisions: Partition depot events and execution state by execution-id.
Microbatch lifecycle owns $$executions with embedded execution state and subindexed claim decisions.
No query topologies: protocol reads use direct PState selects for one execution.
tradeoffs: Embedding bounded DAG state and claims under execution enables local atomic lifecycle decisions and avoids cross-execution scans.
Status is derived from DAG dependencies, success, lease, and current clock rather than a separate global dispatch queue.
seam: No cron, cancellation, failure policy, callbacks, external effect exactly-once guarantee, or job-definition service.
pstates: $$executions keyed by execution-id; state contains DAG/clock/nodes, claims map keyed by claim-id
queries: No query topologies in reference module.
get-execution, get-node, get-claim, get-claimable-nodes use direct foreign-select-one on $$executions.

write: Client appends SubmitExecution, AdvanceClock, Claim, or Complete.
hash-by :execution-id routes to owner; lifecycle microbatch validates DAG or applies ordered transition to that execution's state.
Claim decision and node lease/token update are persisted with execution-local claim history.
read: Client directly selects one execution key from $$executions; helper methods derive node status or fetch one nested claim.
There is no query topology or cross-partition read path.
flow.partition: execution-id is the depot hash key and the top-level $$executions key; all data for one execution is colocated.

caveat: Workers must make external effects idempotent using effect-id and fencing token. The module coordinates claims and results; triggers and retry policies are excluded.

title: Feature Flag Service
summary: Multi-tenant revisioned whole-configuration flag store with ordered equality targeting, deterministic SHA-256 rollout bucketing, and kill switch.
source: HLD Handbook Feature Flag Service case study, adapted by this repository's bounded challenge contract.
requirements: Store one complete configuration per [tenant env flag-key] and accept only strictly newer revisions.
Evaluate kill switch, safe handling of unknown operators, ordered equality rules, rollout, then default.
Compute stable subject rollout bucket from length-prefixed UTF-8 identity components.
nonfunctional: Evaluation and config reads access only one flag, independent of total flags/tenants/environments.
Bucket computation is deterministic and state-free.
constraints: Revision is positive; rollout threshold is 0..10000.
Bucket is SHA-256 first 8 digest bytes as unsigned big-endian integer modulo 10000; revision excluded.
Any non-:eq rule makes evaluation use off-value unless kill switch already applies.
invariants: Equal or lower revision is a no-op; accepted write replaces the entire configuration.
First matching rule wins; missing subject attribute is a nonmatch.
Killed and unsafe configurations return off-value; no config returns nil/missing.
acceptance: Rollout applies iff bucket < threshold; default result includes bucket only if rollout exists.
Evaluation result carries stored revision except when configuration is missing.
Writes for a flag preserve invocation order; independent flags need no ordering.
environment: Durable flag PState; async writes synchronized before reads
interfaces: create-module returns module and wrap-client; client implements Synchronizable
decisions: Partition writes by FlagId [tenant env flag-key].
Microbatch topology flags stores the current full config in $$flags.
Reads evaluate through direct client PState selects; no query topology is declared.
tradeoffs: Whole-config replacement and per-flag partitioning simplify stale-write ordering and bound reads.
Evaluation happens in client wrapper after one direct state select; no SDK distribution or server-side query topology.
seam: SDK distribution, SSE/CDN, audit, deletion, experiment analytics, mutual exclusion, and capacity are excluded.
pstates: $$flags keyed by FlagId; revision, kill/off/default values, ordered rules, optional rollout
queries: No query topologies in reference module.
get-flag-config/evaluate directly foreign-select-one $$flags; compute-bucket is pure client computation.

write: hash-by :flag-id routes to flag owner; flags microbatch compares revision and replaces $$flags only when greater.
read: get-flag-config/evaluate directly select the one FlagId config from $$flags; evaluate-config applies decision order in client wrapper.
compute-bucket runs locally from four length-prefixed components without a PState read; there is no query topology.
flow.partition: FlagId [tenant env flag-key] is the depot hash key and $$flags top-level key; each flag configuration is colocated.

caveat: Safe fallback covers unknown rule operators, not arbitrary malformed configurations. SDK distribution is excluded.

title: Enterprise RAG System
summary: Tenant-scoped revisioned documents, independent ACL and membership streams, and keyword retrieval that authorizes candidates before top-k truncation.
source: HLD Handbook Enterprise RAG case study, adapted by this repository's bounded challenge contract.
requirements: Replace or tombstone document chunks by monotonic content revision; independently replace ACLs and user groups by their own revisions.
Index tenant-scoped chunk tokens for keyword lookup.
Score by distinct query-token overlap, authorize live document candidates before ranking and truncating.
nonfunctional: Query must not scan documents/chunks without query-token matches or another tenant's data.
Content update work is proportional to that document's old/new chunks; ACL and membership updates must not scale with tenant documents.
constraints: At most 32 chunks per document and 32 tokens per chunk; tokens compare by exact string equality.
Unknown ACL denies; unknown user has no groups; ACL, membership, and content revision streams are independent.
Candidates order by score descending, doc-id ascending, chunk-id ascending; k=0 returns empty.
invariants: Strictly greater revision wins independently per stream; equal/lower is no-op.
Tombstone remains in effect through ACL changes; newer content put revives while retaining existing ACL.
Authorization precedes top-k; only live chunks with intersecting ACL/user groups and positive score are returned.
acceptance: Results include text citation, score, content revision, and ACL revision.
Unknown ACL/user and nonmatching tokens return no result; tenant identity scopes docs, users, and postings.
Document metadata read is nil only when neither content nor ACL exists.
environment: Durable PStates and microbatch entities topology; synchronized asynchronous writes
interfaces: EnterpriseRag: put-document!, delete-document!, put-document-acl!, put-user-groups!, get-document, get-user-groups, query
create-module returns module and wrap-client; client implements Synchronizable
decisions: Partition write stream by typed key; membership and document identity keys include tenant.
entities microbatch maintains separate $$docs, $$chunks, $$users, $$postings; postings keyed by tenant/token and chunk reference.
No query topology: wrapper fetches token postings and candidate doc metadata via direct foreign selects, then scores/authorizes locally.
tradeoffs: Inverted token postings avoid full document scans; writes diff old and new chunk references.
Retrieval reads postings per token and metadata per candidate document. Index maintenance adds write work to reduce query scans.
seam: Connectors/parsers, embeddings/vector index, hybrid reranking, LLM generation, citations validation, caching, admin UI, and capacity are excluded.
pstates: $$docs keyed by DocKey [tenant doc-id]: content/ACL revisions and metadata
$$postings keyed by TokenKey [tenant token], then ChunkRef [doc-id chunk-id]
queries: No query topologies in reference module.
query directly reads one user, matching token postings, and matching document metadata through foreign-select/foreign-select-one; ranking and ACL filtering occur in client wrapper.

write: Client appends content, tombstone, ACL, or membership event to *writes keyed by tenant-scoped DocKey/UserKey.
hash-by :key routes event to owner; entities microbatch enforces the relevant revision fence.
Content replacement updates $$docs/$$chunks and diffs tenant-token references in $$postings; ACL and membership updates do not reindex chunks.
read: query directly selects user membership, then matching [tenant token] postings and candidate [tenant doc-id] metadata; no query topology.
Wrapper filters live/authorized chunks before distinct-token scoring, deterministic sort, and top-k truncation.
flow.partition: Write events hash-by :key. Posting reads use TokenKey [tenant token]; doc metadata/chunks use DocKey [tenant doc-id]. These are different partition keys, so query's direct foreign selects are explicit repartitioning reads, not colocated local selects.

caveat: Sparse keyword retrieval with supplied tokens. ACL authorization precedes top-k; embeddings and generated answers are excluded.
